record.original_question: Let C be a closed Jordan curve. Then if f (z) = z + a2 z 2 + . . ., g(z) = z −1 +b0 +b1 z +. . . map D onto the inside and outside of C respectively, the area principle shows that C is the unit circumference T. If we remove the normalisation on g and replace g by g1 (z) = b−1 z −1 + b0 + b1 z + . . ., what can be said about the connection between f and g1 ? For example, what about the asymptotic behaviour of their coefficients, or their Lipschitz behaviour on T, or about prime ends (if we make C slightly non-Jordan)? (D. A. Brannan)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk and $\mathbb{T}=\partial\mathbb{D}$ the unit circle. Let $C$ be a closed Jordan curve in the plane, and let \[ f(z) = z + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 + \cdots \] be the conformal map of $\mathbb{D}$ onto the bounded component of $\mathbb{C}\setminus C$, and let \[ g_1(z) = b_{-1} z^{-1} + b_0 + b_1 z + b_2 z^2 + \cdots \qquad (b_{-1}\neq 0) \] be a conformal map of $\mathbb{D}$ onto the unbounded component of $\mathbb{C}\setminus C$ (i.e., onto the outside of $C$, including $\infty$, with no normalization imposed on the leading coefficient $b_{-1}$). 

It is classical (via the area principle) that if one further imposes the normalization $b_{-1}=1$ (so that $g(z)=z^{-1}+b_0+b_1 z+\cdots$), then $C$ must be the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$. 

Without that normalization on $g_1$, determine what relationship must hold between the maps $f$ and $g_1$. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Describe the asymptotic behaviour of the Taylor coefficients $\{a_n\}_{n\ge 2}$ of $f$ in terms of those of $g_1$ (and conversely).
\item Describe the Lipschitz (or modulus-of-continuity) behaviour of the boundary extensions of $f$ and $g_1$ on $\mathbb{T}$ in relation to one another.
\item If the Jordan-curve hypothesis on $C$ is relaxed slightly (so that prime ends arise), describe the correspondence between the prime-end structures induced by $f$ and by $g_1$.
\end{enumerate}
